items.stem: In enterprise risk management, 'risk appetite' is best defined as:

options.text: The amount and type of risk an organisation is willing to accept to pursue its objectives
options.rationale: Correct: risk appetite is the level of risk the organisation chooses to take in pursuit of objectives.

options.text: The maximum possible loss the organisation could ever suffer
options.rationale: That is closer to maximum exposure, not chosen appetite.

options.text: The probability that any risk will occur
options.rationale: That describes likelihood, a component of risk assessment, not appetite.

options.text: The cost of the organisation's insurance premiums
options.rationale: Insurance cost is a treatment expense, not risk appetite.

items.explanation: Correct: risk appetite is the level of risk the organisation chooses to take in pursuit of objectives.

items.stem: A company wants to protect against a rise in the price of a commodity it must buy in six months. Which instrument most directly hedges this?

options.text: Buying a forward or futures contract to fix the purchase price
options.rationale: Correct: buying forward/futures locks in the purchase price and hedges the upward price risk.

options.text: Selling a forward contract on the commodity
options.rationale: Selling forward hedges a seller, not a buyer facing rising prices.
Share buybacks do not hedge commodity price risk.
Dividend policy is unrelated to commodity price hedging.

items.explanation: Correct: buying forward/futures locks in the purchase price and hedges the upward price risk.
